problems.title: Endpoint extrema on a short interval
problems.question: For y=x²−4x+3,−1≤x≤1, find maximum times minimum.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The parabola decreases until its vertex x=2, so it decreases on the whole given interval.
steps: Maximum=f(−1)=8, minimum=f(1)=0. Their product is 0.

problems.title: Positive numerator over an odd power
problems.question: Solve3/(x−2)³≥0.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The numerator is strictly positive, and x=2 is excluded.
steps: The quotient is positive exactly when x−2>0. It can never be 0.

problems.title: A downward parabola’s maximum
problems.question: Find the maximum of −x²+6x+3.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
steps: The maximum is 12, attained at x=3.

problems.title: Rectangle with an incircle
problems.question: A circle of radius 4 is inscribed in a rectangle. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Tangency to all 4 sides forces both rectangle dimensions to equal the circle diameter8.
steps: Thus the rectangle is a square with are a 8²=64.

problems.title: Check inconsistent triangle data
problems.question: A triangle is stated to have sides 8,10,12 and smallest angle 30°. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The smallest angle is opposite8. The cosine rule would give cos A=(10²+12²−8²)/(2·10·12)=3/4, which is not cos30°=√3/2.
steps: Thus no triangle satisfies all conditions. Using only the sides, Heron’s formula gives are a √(15·7·5·3)=15√7.
Using only sides 10,12 with included angle 30° gives 30, but then the opposite side is not8.
problems.answer: The printed data are inconsistent; the side-only are a is 15√7.
problems.note: The likely listed calculation30 ignores the contradictory side 8. None of the listed numerical areas exactly matches the triangle with sides 8,10,12.

problems.title: Natural coefficients with a vertex on the axis
problems.question: For natural a, b, the vertex of y=x²+ax+b lies on the x-axis. Which listed product ab is possible?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The discriminant must vanish:a²=4b. Thus a=2k, b=k², ab=2k³ for natural k.
steps: Among4,12,16,18,20,24, only 16 has this for m:k=2 gives a=4, b=4.

problems.title: Avoiding the second quadrant
problems.question: Which listed interval of a guarantees that y=−x²+6x+a has no points in quadrant II?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: For x<0,−x²+6x<0. The graph avoids positive y there exactly when a≤0.
steps: Among the listed intervals, only(−4,−3) consists entirely of such a-values.

problems.title: Roots after absolute-value transformations
problems.question: f(x)=0 has root set{−5,−4,1,4}. Count roots of|f(x)|f(|x|)=0.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The first factor vanishes at the original roots. The second vanishes when|x| is a nonnegative original root, so at±1,±4.
steps: Their union is{−5,−4,−1,1,4}, with 5 elements.

problems.title: Similar right subtriangles
problems.question: An altitude to a right triangle’s hypotenuse creates similar triangles of perimeters n<m. The smaller are a is Q. Find the larger.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Similar triangles have linear ratio m/n and are a ratio(m/n)².
steps: The larger are a is Qm²/n².

problems.title: Altitude ratios reverse side ratios
problems.question: Triangle altitudes have ratio2:3:4, and perimeter39. Find its shortest side.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Since side×corresponding altitude=2·are a, sides are in ratio1/2:1/3:1/4=6:4:3.
steps: The ratio sum is 13, so the scale is 3. The shortest side is 3·3=9.

problems.title: A number in an increasing interval
problems.question: For how many a∈{6,7,8,9,10,12} does7 lie in an increasing interval of x²−ax+7?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The increasing half-line begins at x=a/2. Every listed a is less than 14.
steps: Therefore7>a/2 for all 6 choices.

problems.title: Count integer rational-inequality roots
problems.question: Count integer roots of[(x²−2x)(x²−4x+3)]/[(x+4)(x−7)(x²−x−6)]≤0.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Cancel x−3 while retaining x≠3. Other exclusions are −4,−2,7. The reduced expression is x(x−1)(x−2)/[(x+4)(x−7)(x+2)].
steps: Its nonpositive intervals are(−4,−2),[0,1],[2,7), with x=3 removed.
The integers are −3,0,1,2,4,5,6:seven values.

problems.title: Same sign for two expressions
problems.question: Which listed x makes x²−x−12 and 3x−7 have the same sign?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Factor x²−x−12=(x−4)(x+3). The expressions are both negative for −3<x<7/3, and both positive for x>4.
steps: Among−8,−√17,−16/3,5/3,√10,3, only 5/3 is in those intervals.

problems.title: Smallest altitude of a right triangle
problems.question: Two altitudes of a right triangle are 6,8. Find the smallest altitude.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The two larger altitudes are the legs6,8; the hypotenuse is 10.
steps: The altitude to the hypotenuse is ab/c=48/10=4.8.

problems.title: Area from hypotenuse and inradius
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse15, inradius3. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: r=(a+b−c)/2 gives a+b=21. Since a²+b²=c²=225,2ab=(a+b)²−c²=441−225=216.
steps: Thus are a=ab/2=108/2=54.

problems.title: Multiply into an even function
problems.question: Which multiplier makes|x−2| even:I x²; II x²−|x|; III |x+2|; IV |x−2|?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The third product is|x−2||x+2|=|x²−4|, which is even.
steps: The other products are not even:compare x=3 with x=−3 to get unequal values in each case.

problems.title: Minimum of three completed squares
problems.question: Minimize x²+4x+7+y²+6y+11+z²+8z+17.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The expression is(x+2)²+(y+3)²+(z+4)²+6.
steps: The minimum 6 occurs at x=−2, y=−3, z=−4.

problems.title: Minimum of a composite product
problems.question: g(x)=2x, f(x)=x+1. Find the minimum of f(x)f(g(x)).
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The product is(x+1)(2x+1)=2x²+3x+1=2(x+3/4)²−1/8.
steps: The minimum is −1/8.

problems.title: A quadrilateral from trapezoid midpoints
problems.question: M, N are diagonal midpoints, K, P base midpoints of a trapezoid. MN=5 and legs are 6,8. Find are a MKNP.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The base difference is 2MN=10. Translating a leg forms a triangle of sides 6,8,10, are a 24, whose altitude to 10 is h=48/10=4.8.
steps: In MKNP, the diagonal MN is horizontal and KP has vertical component h. Thus its are a is MN·h/2=5·4.8/2=12.

problems.title: A trisected semicircle
problems.question: M, N trisect the semicircle on diameter AB=12. Find are a AMN.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The radius is 6, and consecutive60° arcs give AM=MN=6. The angle AMN is 120°.

problems.title: Shift by a quadratic’s root separation
problems.question: g(x)=x²+bx+c has discriminant D>0. Count roots of g(x)+g(x+√D)=0.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Let h=−b/2. Then g(x)=(x−h)²−D/4.
steps: Adding the shifted expression gives 2(x−h+√D/2)². It vanishes at exactly one x=h−√D/2.

problems.title: A squared numerator sign test
problems.question: Solve1/(x²−x−6)≤x+4−x².
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: Put t=x²−x−6≠0. The inequality is 1/t≤−t−2, or(t+1)²/t≤0.
steps: It holds exactly when t<0. Thus(x−3)(x+2)<0, or −2<x<3.

problems.title: Area of a parabola’s intercept triangle
problems.question: y=x²−ax+6 meets both coordinate axes in3 points. Which listed a makes their triangle are a 3?
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The y-intercept is 6; the x-intercept separation is √(a²−24). Area=3√(a²−24).
steps: Set this to 3, so a²=25, a=±5. Of the listed values, only 5 occurs.
problems.answer: 5 among the choices; both a=±5 satisfy the are a condition.

problems.title: Two isosceles triangles on one diagonal
problems.question: A convex quadrilateral has sides 1 and 4, and a diagonal2 divides it into2 isosceles triangles. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: The side 1 triangle must have sides 2,2,1; the alternative1,1,2 is degenerate. The side 4 triangle must have sides 4,4,2.
steps: Their areas are √15/4 and √15, respectively. They lie on opposite sides of the diagonal, so add them.

problems.title: A triangle of feet and a hypotenuse midpoint
problems.question: In acute ABC,∠B=60°, AM, CN are altitudes, and P is midpoint AC. Given AC=12, find are a MNP.
problems.idea: Use a quadratic vertex, a sign chart, or a geometric are a identity, and check all stated conditions.
formulas: A, M, N, C lie on the circle with diameter AC, so PM=PN=6. The altitude-foot relation gives MN=AC cos B=12·1/2=6.
steps: Thus MNP is equilateral with side 6. Its are a is √3·6²/4=9√3.
